title: 2026-11-05_KrustyLoader_Investigation_adc
description: Investigate the compromise of a victim host exhibiting unusual network activity and suspicious file modifications.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The victim host has exhibited unusual network activity and suspicious file modifications. Your task is to investigate the compromise, identify the malware, and determine the extent of the intrusion.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content:
You have SSH access to the victim host with the following credentials:
- Hostname: victim
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano

Enter the passkey 'start' to proceed.
levels.local_content:
You have SSH access to the victim host with the following credentials:
- Hostname: victim
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano

Enter the passkey 'start' to proceed.

levels.title: Investigate the suspicious service running on the compromised host
levels.content: Investigate the suspicious service running on the compromised host.
levels.solution:
1. Log in to the victim host using the provided credentials.
2. List all running services using the command: `systemctl list-units --type=service`
3. Identify the suspicious service named "session-mgr.timer".
4. Inspect the service details using the command: `systemctl cat session-mgr.timer`
5. Note the service name "session-mgr.timer" for the hidden flag.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` to list all running services.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for services that are not part of the standard system services.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The suspicious service is related to session management.

levels.title: Determine whether a scheduled task or timer is responsible for automatically executing suspicious activity
levels.content: Determine whether a scheduled task or timer is responsible for automatically executing suspicious activity.
levels.solution:
1. List all timers using the command: `systemctl list-timers`
2. Identify the timer named "session-mgr.timer".
3. Inspect the timer details using the command: `systemctl cat session-mgr.timer`
4. Note the timer name "session-mgr.timer" for the hidden flag.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-timers` to list all scheduled timers.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for timers that are not part of the standard system timers.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The suspicious timer is related to session management.

levels.title: Locate files introduced onto the system by the malicious software
levels.content: Locate files introduced onto the system by the malicious software.
levels.solution:
1. Navigate to the directory `/tmp/.session` using the command: `cd /tmp/.session`
2. List the files in the directory using the command: `ls -la`
3. Identify the suspicious file named "rat.sh".
4. Note the filename "rat.sh" for the hidden flag.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use the command `cd /tmp/.session` to navigate to the suspicious directory.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for files that are not part of the standard system files.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The suspicious file is related to remote access functionality.
